sanjay: ran an nsys + perfetto combo on the 2.3.1 serving image, reproduced a latency spike during steady-state traffic. attaching trace link: https://redwood-internal/nsys/2356784321.nsys :eyes:

sanjay: quick summary — midbatch eviction + kv-cache refills coincide with repeated cuBLASLt algo probes. the timeline shows a ~30ms hiccup every ~120ms window, correlates with cudamalloc async stalls and algo workspace allocation churn.

devin: can you paste the kernel timeline / cublasLt selection log here? curious which algo ids are flapping.

sanjay: sure — clipped timeline and cublaslt log below:
```
# kernel timeline excerpt (perfetto)
00:00:00.000 matmul_128x128x8 (algo=13) 0.96ms
00:00:00.120 matmul_1024x768 (algo=7 workspace=0 fallback->probe) 31.4ms  <-- spike
00:00:00.240 matmul_128x128x8 (algo=13) 0.98ms
00:00:00.360 matmul_1024x768 (algo=7 probe workspace=32MB cudamalloc_async wait) 29.8ms
```
```
# cublasLt selection log (serving runtime debug)
[2026-03-18 10:12:01] probe: matmul shape=(1024,768) tried algo=7 ws=0 -> fails, trying algo=12 ws=32MB -> ok
[2026-03-18 10:12:01] kvcache: miss, inserting prefix, midbatch-evict=true
[2026-03-18 10:12:01] batcher: shape window updated, triggering probe for long-shape
[2026-03-18 10:12:01] workspace-alloc: cudamalloc_async fallback -> synchronous path
```

sanjay: the pattern is: first request for large shape does a cheap algo with zero workspace, then the probe runs needing workspace which forces cudamalloc paths and stalls other kernels. when kv-cache do a refill during that window it nudges the batcher shape distribution and increases probe frequency.

lucy: hmm that matches a regression I saw in commit d3c4a2b — the allocator introduced a slab bypass for smaller allocations, but the threshold math accidentally punts some mid-size ws requests to cudaMallocAsync instead of pooled arena. could definitely cause the synchronous fallback.

perf-bot: perf regression alert: p99 latency +18% for /generate under concurrency=32 (baseline 9ms -> 10.6ms). regression blamelist: d3c4a2b..d6f8e10.

devin: nice find. two quick mitigation paths: 1) widen the warmup window so the batcher learns the large-shape distribution before probing (reduce probe frequency), 2) preselect cublasLt algos for common long shapes at startup so probes don't run mid-traffic.

sanjay: I ran a cheap experiment: set REDWOOD_GEMM_PRESELECT=1 and REDWOOD_GEMM_MAX_PROBE_RATE=0.05 — spike frequency dropped and p99 improved back to ~9.6ms. details: https://redwood-internal/plays/2356784321/exp1.log

lucy: long-term we should fix allocator thresholds. short-term patch: bump slab-bypass threshold from 16MB -> 64MB in allocator (PR queued: https://git.redwood/infrakit/pulls/482). also add a safety to prefer preselected algo if probe would require >16MB WS.

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-1192: "cudamalloc_async fallback causing matmul probe stalls" with attached nsys trace.

devin: can someone run a repro with --nvtx=1 and with CUFFT/CUBLAS env logs enabled, then share timeline? want to see whether other kernels are impacted (softplus/gelu).

sanjay: on it — kicking off a 1hr run in staging with nvtx+verbose logs, will post nsys link when done.

lucy: thanks — if staging repro is clean, we can backport the allocator threshold change to the 2.3.x maintenance branch and roll a canary. :thumbsup:
